extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental scientists, and readers of Baconian natural philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: A systematic taxonomy of 'motions' or active powers in nature used to analyze predominance/submission of forces and to guide experimental investigation of natural phenomena. The list situates each motion with definitions, examples, and experimental implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances of quantity (doses of nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances which measure powers by the quantity of bodies and point out the effect of quantity on the degree of power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: some powers only subsist in universal quantities (earth fixed, tides in seas); many powers act differently with greater or lesser quantity (large masses of water foul less easily than small; new wine ripens differently in small skins vs large casks). One must inquire into the exact proportion of quantity requisite for a given effect rather than assume simple linear ratios (e.g. heavier bullets do not fall proportionally faster). Measures must be determined by experiment, and investigators should guard against estimating doses too high or too low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrestling instances (instances of predominance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that point out the predominance and submission of powers compared with each other — which powers are more energetic/superior or more weak/inferior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when motions and effects are compounded, decomposed, or combined; requires exhibiting principal kinds of motions so their comparative strength may be determined. This classification supports experiments to detect which power predominates in mixed or competing circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of resistance of matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion inherent in every particle that prevents its annihilation; the axiom that two bodies cannot exist in the same place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This motion is ubiquitous and needs no examples for recognition; it underlies inability to reduce matter to nothing by pressure, heat, time, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of connection (to prevent a vacuum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bodies do not allow themselves to be separated at any point from the contact of another body; a tendency to mutual connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: water drawn up by suction or a syringe, cupping, water remaining in perforated jars unless air admitted. Identified with the prevention of vacuum; experimentally visible in suction and capillary-like phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: Bodies strive to deliver themselves from unnatural pressure or tension and to restore dimensions suited to their mass (rebound from compression or tension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: swimming, flying, springs of watches, children's popguns (compressed air ejecting pellets), recoil of stretched strings/cloth. Distinguish from resistance and connection; it is a desire to preserve specific density or form and explains mechanical motion as relaxation from compression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of matter (opposed to motion of liberty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bodies are anxious to acquire a new volume or dimension and attempt it willingly and rapidly (expansion/contraction driven by heat or cold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: heated air dilating, water freezing into ice and crystal under intense cold. Heat and cold act as instruments of this motion; not simply a return to former state but a fresh change toward a new form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: A body's tendency to preserve its own continuity (resistance to solution of continuity) — cohesion within the same body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations: bubbles, round drops, thin threads of dripping water, cohesion of glutinous substances; evident when attempting to separate to very small particles (pestle in mortar, penetration of air into solid vessels). Stronger in hard bodies, faint in liquids but never null.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of acquisition (motion of need)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bodies in the presence of heterogeneous/hostile neighbors seize and unite with other more analogous bodies; a tendency to acquire suitable neighbors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: gold leaf adhering to paper/finger rather than air; paper and cloth imbibing water by expelling air from pores; sugar/sponge absorbing water. Practical rule for dissolution: if a body more adapted to a solid is presented, the solid opens/dissolves to receive it. Also relates to electric-like effects from friction preferring tangible substances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of greater congregation (natural motion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bodies are borne toward masses of similar nature (e.g., heavy bodies toward earth, light toward heaven); a slow, weak, perpetual tendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Called natural motion by the schools; it is weak and slow and can be obscured by other active motions. Errors in its estimate are common; predominance depends on the presence/absence of other motions and mass of body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of lesser congregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Homogeneous parts in any body separate from the heterogeneous and unite together; homogeneous parts coalesce and tend toward each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cream rising in milk, dregs/tartar sinking in wine. Differs from motion of acquisition: (1) lesser congregation unites by affinity without hostile body; (2) produces closer, more selective union. Its action is confined by (a) torpor/sluggishness (overcome by heat, similar active bodies, or vigorous motion), (b) power of a predominant body (e.g., active spirit preventing decomposition), and (c) external motion/agitation (which prevents putrefaction by disturbing subtle congregative motions). Also leads to induration/desiccation when moisture/spirits escape and parts draw together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnetic motion
rubrics_metrics.description: A species of congregation operating at great distances and on great masses; intermediate and imperfectly congregative, raising/swelling without contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguished because it neither begins in contact nor ends in contact; invoked for phenomena like the moon raising waters, stellar attractions, and planetary influences. Treat experimentally with care because it acts at distance and may not fit other congregative categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposed to lesser congregation: bodies avoid, disperse, or refuse to unite with hostile substances; an antipathy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: rejection of fetid smells by the nose, bitter tastes rejected by palate, excrements; certain substances prevent quicksilver reunification (spittle, lard); oil and water refusing to mix due partly to affinity, not only weight differences. Avoidance may be more marked than union in many cases and may contribute to phenomena like antiperistasis (local increases of heat/cold).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of assimilation (self-multiplication/simple generation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Homogeneous bodies convert allied or prepared bodies into their own substance and nature — propagation of a body's nature into others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: flame multiplying over vapors and oils, air generating more air over watery substances, animal/vegetable spirits assimilating juices to form parts. Distinct from mere separation theories of nutrition; applies in animate and inanimate contexts (e.g., flame, air). Accretion (mud between stones hardening, scaly substance around teeth) is related.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of excitement
rubrics_metrics.description: A diffusive, communicative motion that proceeds by art, insinuation, and invitation — it multiplies powers rather than transforming the substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguished from assimilation: excitement invites the excited toward the exciting body's nature and multiplies/changes powers (heat, magnetic power, putrefaction) in the excited body. Examples: heat exciting motion in other bodies without transferring original heat; magnet inducing disposition in iron; leaven/yeast exciting dough/beer/cheese/human body. Excitement depends on predisposition and yielding of the excited body; occurs less readily in dense substances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of impression
rubrics_metrics.description: A subtile, diffusive motion dependent on the first agent such that removal of the agent causes immediate failure; acts quickly and transiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike assimilation or excitement, impression depends on continual presence of the first agent and quickly ceases when removed. Examples: rays of light (colors disappear when light removed), percussions of sounds (sound ceases when vibration/stopped), magnetic attraction in communication where removal of magnet causes iron to fall. Reverberation is repetition, not persistence of a single identical impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of configuration or position
rubrics_metrics.description: Bodies desire particular situations, collocations, or configurations with others (a tendency to a peculiar position rather than union/separation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to abstruse phenomena: why heavens revolve in particular direction/poles; polarity/variation of compass needle; arrangement of fibres/hairs in solids; eddies in liquids equalizing pressure seen as motion of liberty. Requires investigation for control and workmanship of bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of transmission or passage
rubrics_metrics.description: Powers of bodies are impeded or advanced by the medium according to the medium's nature; one medium adapts to light, another to sound, heat, magnetic action, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This motion accounts for how effects are carried through media and how different media favor different actions; experimental attention should be paid to medium properties when testing powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royal or political motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Predominant or governing parts of any body check, subdue, reduce, and regulate the others — a dominion exercised by ruling part over subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conspicuous in animal spirits: governing spirit tempers other motions and prevents decomposition of blood/urine while present. Present in less degree in other bodies where a predominating part restrains transformation; relevant to wrestling instances where parts within wholes are in hierarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneous motion of revolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Bodies with a tendency to move and placed favorably pursue themselves (revolve) or, if unfavourable, rest or move in straight lines; when favorably situated they move in eternal circular motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nine differentiations: centre about which they move; poles; circumference/orbit distance; velocity; direction (east-west or reverse); deviation from circle by spirals relative to centre; deviation by spirals relative to poles; spacing of spirals; variation of poles. Associated with heavenly bodies and subject to disputes (e.g., earth's motion); experimental manipulation limited (cannot experimentally remove moon or earth).
